lines.speaker: Lyle Mercury
lines.text: Welcome aboard Tiki Satellite, one hundred and twelve megacycles! The year is nineteen fifty eight, and the future is right on schedule.

lines.speaker: Lyle Mercury
lines.text: Tiki Satellite. Vibraphone, bongos, and the boundless optimism of the space age. Mind the porthole, folks. That's the Earth.

lines.speaker: Lyle Mercury
lines.text: This is Tiki Satellite, from the Lagoon Deck of Orbital Station Seven. Two hundred miles up, and still looking up.

lines.speaker: Lyle Mercury
lines.text: Good morning from Tiki Satellite! The sun has risen. It'll rise again in ninety minutes. That's orbit, friends. Plenty of mornings for everybody.

lines.speaker: Lyle Mercury
lines.text: Tiki Satellite. The theremin is warming up, and the future has never looked brighter. Or more like nineteen fifty eight.

lines.speaker: Lyle Mercury
lines.text: By nineteen sixty five, every family will live in orbit. I know, because I saw it in a magazine, and the magazine had a painting of it.

lines.speaker: Lyle Mercury
lines.text: A lovely family, in a lovely wheel, with a lovely dog floating gently past a picture window. We're just a little early, that's all. Somebody has to plump the cushions.

lines.speaker: Lyle Mercury
lines.text: A word about the relief crew. They're expected any day now. They've been expected any day now for quite a while.

lines.speaker: Lyle Mercury
lines.text: I'm sure they're simply held up in traffic. By now there must be thousands of stations just like this one. Bigger. Shinier. Possibly with two lagoons.

lines.speaker: Lyle Mercury
lines.text: A listener has written in, and I'll read the letter in full. Dear Lyle. It is not nineteen fifty eight.

lines.speaker: Lyle Mercury
lines.text: Well! Thank you for writing, sir. That's a very interesting point of view, and we'll certainly look into it. Possibly by nineteen sixty five. Here's a cha cha.

lines.speaker: Lyle Mercury
lines.text: That was Howard, on the bird calls. There are no birds in orbit. There may never be. Howard has never let that stop him.

lines.speaker: Lyle Mercury
lines.text: He says that when the birds of tomorrow do come up here, and they will, they'll want to hear something familiar.

lines.speaker: Lyle Mercury
lines.text: On the theremin tonight, Miss Vera Voss. She plays it without touching it at all, which our engineers find very reassuring.

lines.speaker: Lyle Mercury
lines.text: Nobody touches anything on Station Seven without the training. That's the future, folks. Hands off, and humming.

lines.speaker: Lyle Mercury
lines.text: Another sunrise has just come up over the edge of the Earth. That's our eleventh today, and we toast every one.

lines.speaker: Lyle Mercury
lines.text: Some of the crew are getting very cheerful. So is the sun. Here's a number for sunrise twelve.

lines.speaker: Lyle Mercury
lines.text: Tonight's programme comes to you courtesy of Grumbel's Ladders. In nineteen sixty three, Grumbel's will build the first ladder to the moon.

lines.speaker: Lyle Mercury
lines.text: I've seen the drawings. It leans against the moon at a jaunty angle. Grumbel's Ladders. Up is a choice!

lines.speaker: Lyle Mercury
lines.text: Hello down there to the operator on the relay ship. My, what a modern looking vessel. Is that what they'll all look like, by nineteen sixty five?

lines.speaker: Lyle Mercury
lines.text: Don't tell me. I like to be surprised. Come aboard for a cocktail any time. Dock at the round door. They're all round.

lines.speaker: Lyle Mercury
lines.text: We had a visitor this week. A shadow who called himself Greg. No pressure suit, no ticket. Just walked in through the porthole.

lines.speaker: Lyle Mercury
lines.text: In the future, I expect shadows will travel freely between the planets. Greg is simply ahead of his time. Like the rest of us.

lines.speaker: Lyle Mercury
lines.text: Tired of cooking? Then let the atom do it! The Halcyon Atomic Kitchen roasts a chicken in four seconds, washes the dishes with a gentle beam of light, and keeps the whole house toasty warm until nineteen seventy one.

lines.speaker: Lyle Mercury
lines.text: Halcyon Atomics. Tomorrow's kitchen, today. Ask your doctor whether a glow is right for you.

lines.speaker: Lyle Mercury
lines.text: Thirsty in zero gravity? Try the Floating Pineapple, the cocktail of tomorrow. Served in a perfect sphere, sipped through a silver straw, and pursued at a leisurely pace around the lounge.

lines.speaker: Lyle Mercury
lines.text: The Floating Pineapple. Ask your bartender. He's on the ceiling.

lines.speaker: Lyle Mercury
lines.text: And now it's time for Tomorrow's Headlines, where we look ahead to the wonderful world of nineteen sixty five.

lines.speaker: Lyle Mercury
lines.text: Here's the news from the future, folks. Don't worry. It's all good.

lines.speaker: Lyle Mercury
lines.text: By nineteen sixty five, every household will have a robot butler named Clarence. All of them will be named Clarence. It's simpler that way.

lines.speaker: Lyle Mercury
lines.text: By nineteen sixty three, the weather will be decided by a committee, and the committee will choose sunny. Rain will be available by appointment, on Tuesdays, for the lawns.

lines.speaker: Lyle Mercury
lines.text: By nineteen sixty six, dinner will come in a single pill. Dessert will be a second, smaller pill. The washing up will be a glass of water.

lines.speaker: Lyle Mercury
lines.text: By nineteen sixty five, nobody will ever be lonely again. Everybody will have a wrist radio, and every wrist radio will be tuned to this station.

lines.speaker: Lyle Mercury
lines.text: Those were tomorrow's headlines. Remember, folks. The future is coming, and it's bringing snacks.

lines.speaker: Lyle Mercury
lines.text: Good morning, good morning! This is Breakfast in Orbit, on Tiki Satellite. Breakfast this morning is a pill. Lunch is a slightly larger pill. Let's have some vibraphone.

lines.speaker: Lyle Mercury
lines.text: Today's breakfast pill tastes of pancakes, bacon and a sense of purpose. If yours tastes of nothing, you've taken the vitamin.

lines.speaker: Lyle Mercury
lines.text: Take another one. It's the future. There's plenty.

lines.speaker: Lyle Mercury
lines.text: Up here the sun sets sixteen times a day, so the cocktail hour comes round rather often. Welcome to the Cocktail Hour of Tomorrow, on Tiki Satellite.

lines.speaker: Lyle Mercury
lines.text: A note from the bar. Please hold your drink with both hands, and don't let go of it.

lines.speaker: Lyle Mercury
lines.text: In zero gravity, a cocktail you let go of is a cocktail you will meet again. Perhaps on Thursday. Perhaps on somebody's hat.

lines.speaker: Lyle Mercury
lines.text: Moonlight on the Lagoon Deck. The water's going round the wheel, the moon's going round the Earth, and the bongos are going round in my head. Lovely.

lines.speaker: Lyle Mercury
lines.text: Late on the station, and the lagoon has gone very still, in a ring all the way around us, the way lagoons will be in the future.

lines.speaker: Lyle Mercury
lines.text: The moon is so close tonight you could almost reach it. By nineteen sixty five, you will. Bring a scarf.

lines.speaker: Lyle Mercury
lines.text: Halloween aboard Station Seven! The crew have carved a pumpkin of tomorrow. It's chrome, it glows, and it orbits the lounge every forty minutes.

lines.speaker: Lyle Mercury
lines.text: Our scientists say that by nineteen sixty five, every pumpkin will glow all by itself. They're working on it in the lab. Something in the lab is glowing already.

lines.speaker: Lyle Mercury
lines.text: Folks, it seems a moon has gone missing. Now, don't be alarmed. By nineteen sixty five there'll be so many moons, nobody will miss one.

lines.speaker: Lyle Mercury
lines.text: Our engineers are building three spares as we speak.

lines.speaker: Lyle Mercury
lines.text: That aroma drifting through the station is toast. And not ordinary toast, friends. Atomic toast, done on both sides in an instant.

lines.speaker: Lyle Mercury
lines.text: Somebody out there has the kitchen of tomorrow!

lines.speaker: Lyle Mercury
lines.text: Everybody aboard is humming the same tune, and nobody can finish it.

lines.speaker: Lyle Mercury
lines.text: Not to worry. Scientists predict that by nineteen sixty four, every song will finish itself, automatically.

lines.speaker: Lyle Mercury
lines.text: Three knocks on the airlock! Come in, come in!

lines.speaker: Lyle Mercury
lines.text: Nobody there. We're two hundred miles up. Well, that's the future for you. Always dropping by before it's ready.

lines.speaker: Lyle Mercury
lines.text: Look at that porthole! The sky has turned a colour I've never seen before.

lines.speaker: Lyle Mercury
lines.text: Mark my words, folks. By nineteen sixty two, that colour will be on every refrigerator in the land.

lines.speaker: Lyle Mercury
lines.text: A pigeon has come aboard Station Seven! No pressure suit, no ticket, perfectly calm.

lines.speaker: Lyle Mercury
lines.text: Folks, this is the pigeon of tomorrow. And frankly, it seems to know me.
